summary: Robert Hayes, age 59, has applied for a $500,000 15-year term life policy at the Preferred Non-Tobacco rate, but the case shows significant unresolved medical and disclosure issues. He has a documented history of coronary artery disease with a drug-eluting stent, poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.8%), uncontrolled hypertension, obesity, dyslipidemia, and a family history of early cardiac death, all of which materially elevate mortality risk. There is also a direct conflict between his declared non-smoker status and lab findings (positive cotinine and elevated carboxyhemoglobin) plus APS notes of recent smoking cessation, calling the requested preferred non-tobacco rate class into question. An active PRN nitroglycerin prescription further conflicts with the APS statement of no angina in the past 12 months, suggesting possible unreported symptoms. Key objective evidence — recent EKG/stress test results, cardiology follow-up notes, confirmed smoking status, and income verification — is missing and needed before classification can be finalized.

draft_rationale.rationale: This case presents multiple high-severity medical risk flags (established coronary artery disease with stent, poorly controlled diabetes, and probable undisclosed tobacco use) compounded by moderate flags (uncontrolled hypertension, obesity, dyslipidemia, family history of early cardiac death). Two unresolved conflicts — the tobacco use discrepancy affecting the requested preferred non-tobacco rate class, and the angina/nitroglycerin discrepancy potentially indicating unreported symptomatic coronary disease — directly bear on both risk classification and rate class eligibility. Critical missing information (recent EKG/stress test, cardiology follow-up notes, confirmed smoking status, and income verification) prevents a confident assessment of current mortality risk. Given the complexity and materiality of these open issues, this draft leans toward referral to a senior underwriter for further review rather than a final approval or decline determination; a human underwriter should validate this direction once outstanding items are addressed.
